questions.stem: What is the key architectural difference between Sharding and Partitioning?
options: Sharding divides columns whereas partitioning divides rows
Sharding stores each shard on one dedicated node, giving a shared-nothing architecture, whereas partitions may share a node
Sharding keeps all data on a single node whereas partitioning spreads it
Sharding does not divide tables into smaller datasets
Sharding only works on NoSQL databases
questions.explanation: Both divide tables into smaller datasets, but sharding places each shard on its own dedicated node, which is why it is called shared-nothing architecture.

questions.stem: How does key-based sharding decide which shard should hold newly written data?
options: By assigning shards in round-robin order
By consulting a manually maintained lookup table
By sorting the data into ranges of a given value
By plugging a value taken from the new data into a hash function
By writing to the shard with the most free space
questions.explanation: Key-based, also called hash-based, sharding takes a value from the new data and runs it through a hash function to determine the destination shard.

questions.stem: Which sharding architecture divides data according to ranges of a given value?
options: Range-based sharding
Key-based sharding
Directory-based sharding
Hash-based sharding
Vertical sharding
questions.explanation: Range-based sharding shards data based on ranges of a given value.

questions.stem: What must be created and maintained for directory-based sharding?
options: A hash function for the shard key
A range table for each column
A replica of every shard on every node
A single master node that holds all writes
A lookup table that uses a shard key to track which shard holds which data
questions.explanation: Directory-based sharding relies on a lookup table keyed by the shard key that records where each piece of data lives.

questions.stem: What is described as the main appeal of sharding a database?
options: It reduces storage costs by compressing data
It removes the need for indexes
It facilitates horizontal scaling, also known as scaling out
It makes the database easier to return to an unsharded state
It guarantees strict consistency across nodes
questions.explanation: The main appeal of sharding is that it helps facilitate horizontal scaling, or scaling out.

options: Adding more machines to an existing stack to spread out the load and allow more traffic and faster processing
Upgrading a single server with more memory and CPU
Splitting a table's columns into separate tables
Moving a database to faster storage
Reducing the number of nodes to cut cost
questions.explanation: Horizontal scaling means adding more machines to the existing stack to spread the load, allowing more traffic and faster processing.

questions.stem: How does sharding help make an application more reliable?
options: Every shard holds a full copy of the data
Shards are automatically rebalanced after every write
Sharded databases never need backups
An outage is likely to affect only a single shard, so the overall impact is less than if the whole database crashed
Sharding prevents data corruption entirely
questions.explanation: With a sharded database an outage typically affects just one shard, mitigating the impact compared with an entire database going down.

questions.stem: Which statement is NOT a drawback of sharding?
options: If done incorrectly, it can lead to lost data or corrupted tables
It is natively supported by every database engine
A sharded database can become unbalanced
It is very difficult to return to an unsharded architecture
Backups made before sharding will not include data written since
questions.explanation: One real drawback is that sharding is NOT natively supported by every database engine; the other four statements are genuine drawbacks.

questions.stem: What is the problem with database backups made before the database was sharded?
options: They cannot be restored at all
They become corrupted by the sharding process
They double in size
They are automatically deleted
They will not include data written since the sharding took place
questions.explanation: Any backups taken before sharding will not contain the data written after the database was split.

questions.stem: In the yearly Salary example, why is a query for years 2 and 3 faster on a sharded database than on a standard partitioned one?
options: The sharded database keeps both years in memory
The sharded database has fewer rows
Each node holding a shard processes its own dataset individually, rather than several partitions sharing one node
The sharded query skips the index
Shards are always smaller than partitions
questions.explanation: With one shard per node, each node processes its dataset independently, whereas in shared architecture several partitions may sit on a single node.
